title_en: Life-changing MS Drug to Help People Walk Now on NHS in England
title_zh: 改善行走的MS药物已在英格兰NHS上市
summary_zh: 英国国家医疗服务体系（NHS）在英格兰批准了一种名为法普利啶的多发性硬化症（MS）药物，该药能增强神经信号，帮助部分患者改善行走能力，预计每年约5000名符合条件的患者可受益。患者需试用一个月，仅对“明显有效”者继续供药。此前该药因成本效益考量曾被拒，但在威尔士等地已可用。患者Aysen Slack曾自费购药，此次决定被指“极大改变”生活。
reading_passage:
Aysen Slack says she used to pay for the drug privately until it became too costly

The first drug to help people with multiple sclerosis walk is being made available on the NHS in England.

Fampridine boosts nerve signals to make it easier for some people to move and live independently.

Aysen Slack, who used to pay for fampridine privately until it became too costly, said the decision would make a "huge difference".

Up to 5,000 people in England could benefit each year. The drug is already available elsewhere in the UK.

Multiple sclerosis is caused by the immune system attacking the protective covering around nerve cells - known as myelin.

This damage impairs the ability of nerves to carry electrical messages from the brain to the rest of the body - including those needed for the precise control of muscles needed to walk.

Fampridine is known as a "signal booster" as it helps those electrical messages still get through.

Clinical trials showed around four in 10 people taking the drug had improvements in their walking speed and in how long they could walk for.

This could be the difference between getting around the house or needing help at home or enabling people to go out and see friends and family.

Current NHS support includes physiotherapy and walking aids.

The drug has previously been rejected for use by the NHS in England as it was not considered value for money, although it did become available in Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.

Aysen Slack, 65 and from Eastbourne, chose to pay privately for the pills once she heard about them.

She said fampridine was "working well for me" but came at a "significant expense and I could not keep doing that forever" so she had to stop.

Slack said it was "great news" the drug was coming to the NHS and she "would definitely like to try" again.

"My mobility has decreased a lot and even in my flat I have to use sticks now," she said, "it would make a huge difference to my life if I were able to improve my walking."

More than 120,000 people live with MS in England. However, only around 5,000 people a year will be eligible - based on the extent of their walking difficulties.

Patients will try the medicine for up to a month and only those showing "clear benefit" will be able to continue taking it.

Prof Frankie Swords, the NHS national medical director, said: "Walking difficulties can have a huge impact on the freedom and independence of people with MS, so this signal-boosting pill could be life-changing for thousands of patients.

"Even a modest improvement could mean getting around the house more easily, going out with greater confidence and living more independently."

Ceri Smith, from the MS Society, said they were "delighted" by the news as the drug could be "life-changing" for many, allowing people to "live more independently or stay in employment".

difficult_sentences.sentence: This damage impairs the ability of nerves to carry electrical messages from the brain to the rest of the body - including those needed for the precise control of muscles needed to walk.
difficult_sentences.explanation_zh: 本句主干为'This damage impairs the ability...'; 破折号后为补充说明成分'including those...', 其中'needed for...'为过去分词短语作定语修饰'those', 说明所需神经信号的类型。
difficult_sentences.grammar_point: 破折号引出插入语，过去分词短语作定语
difficult_sentences.translation_zh: 这种损伤会损害神经将电信号从大脑传送到身体其他部位的能力——包括那些精准控制行走所需肌肉的信号。

difficult_sentences.sentence: Clinical trials showed around four in 10 people taking the drug had improvements in their walking speed and in how long they could walk for.
difficult_sentences.explanation_zh: 本句主句为'Clinical trials showed...'，后接宾语从句省略that；'taking the drug'为现在分词短语作定语修饰'people'；'improvements in...'后接并列的介词宾语'their walking speed'和名词性从句'how long they could walk for'。
difficult_sentences.grammar_point: 宾语从句，现在分词短语作定语，名词性从句
difficult_sentences.translation_zh: 临床试验显示，大约十分之四服用该药的人在步行速度和行走持续时间上都有所改善。

difficult_sentences.sentence: The drug has previously been rejected for use by the NHS in England as it was not considered value for money, although it did become available in Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.
difficult_sentences.explanation_zh: 本句主干为'The drug has...been rejected...'; 'as'引导原因状语从句；'although'引导让步状语从句，其中'did become'为强调结构。
difficult_sentences.grammar_point: 原因状语从句，让步状语从句，强调结构
difficult_sentences.translation_zh: 该药此前因不被认为物有所值而被英格兰NHS拒绝使用，尽管它在威尔士、苏格兰和北爱尔兰已可提供。

difficult_sentences.sentence: Patients will try the medicine for up to a month and only those showing 'clear benefit' will be able to continue taking it.
difficult_sentences.explanation_zh: 本句为并列句，由'and'连接两个分句；第二个分句中'those'为主语，'showing 'clear benefit''为现在分词短语作定语修饰'those'，意为'只有那些显示出明显获益的患者'。
difficult_sentences.grammar_point: 并列句，现在分词短语作定语
difficult_sentences.translation_zh: 患者将试用该药长达一个月，只有显示出'明显益处'的患者才能继续服用。

idioms.meaning_zh: 改变人生的；对生活有重大影响的
idioms.usage_note: 常作形容词，形容某事对个人生活产生深远影响。
idioms.example: The new technology was life-changing for people with disabilities.

idioms.meaning_zh: 需要付出高昂代价；伴随很大开支
idioms.usage_note: 'come at a...expense'表示某事以某种代价为条件，可替换形容词。
idioms.example: Buying a house in the city often comes at a significant expense.

idioms.meaning_zh: 一直做某事（尤其指无法持续的情况）
idioms.usage_note: 'keep doing'表示持续做，加上'forever'强调长时间且不可能持久。
idioms.example: He realized he couldn't keep working 12-hour days forever.

idioms.meaning_zh: 对某人很有效；适合某人
idioms.usage_note: 非正式表达，表示某物或某种方法对某人产生良好效果。
idioms.example: This new diet is working well for me; I've already lost weight.

reading_questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.A: Multiple sclerosis is a serious neurological condition.
options.B: A new MS drug is being made available on the NHS in England, potentially helping many.
options.C: Fampridine is a signal-boosting pill that helps MS patients walk.
options.D: Aysen Slack can now afford her medication.

reading_questions.question: According to the passage, what did Aysen Slack do before the drug was approved on the NHS?

options.A: She received the drug for free through a special program.
options.B: She paid for the drug herself.
options.C: She traveled to Wales to get the drug.

reading_questions.question: What can be inferred from Aysen Slack's statement that the decision would make a "huge difference"?

options.A: She is confident the drug will improve her quality of life.
options.B: She believes the drug is too expensive.
options.C: She wants the drug to be available only for herself.
options.D: She thinks the NHS should have made the decision earlier.

reading_questions.question: In paragraph 3, the word "independently" is closest in meaning to:
What is the author's attitude toward the NHS decision?
Which of the following best describes the organization of the passage?

options.A: It presents a problem and then offers a solution.
options.B: It compares different treatment options for MS.
options.C: It starts with a patient's story and then explains the science.
options.D: It announces the news, provides background, and includes stakeholder reactions.

reading_questions.question: Which of the following would be the most appropriate title for the passage?

options.C: Life-changing MS Drug Available on NHS
options.D: The Cost of Prescription Drugs in England
